claim: In the FAQ example, an io2 Block Express volume provisioned with 40,000 IOPS for an I/O size of 16KB achieves up to 40,000 IOPS at that size; if the I/O size is increased to 256 KB, it achieves up to 16,000 IOPS, because the maximum throughput of 4000 MiB/s is achieved at 16,000 IOPS.

qualifiers.scope: per io2 Block Express volume, FAQ example
qualifiers.condition: a volume provisioned with 40,000 IOPS (FAQ example); I/O size of 256 KB

evidence.quote: If the I/O size is increased to 256 KB, then you will achieve up to 16,000 IOPS, since the maximum throughput of 4000 MiB/s is achieved at 16,000 IOPS.
So, if you have provisioned a volume with 40,000 IOPS for an I/O size of 16KB, it will achieve up to 40,000 IOPS at that size.
